source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 123: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assume the model, tokenizer, precision, runtime build, hardware, serving policy, and a versioned mix of short prompts and long generations are fixed. For variant 123, test the falsifiable hypothesis that the candidate admission/scheduling policy improves goodput by at least 5% at the declared offered load while queue-inclusive P99 end-to-end latency does not increase by more than 10% and answer correctness is non-inferior to baseline. Run a randomized paired crossover: replay identical seeded requests under baseline and candidate, alternate order, isolate background load, warm up and discard a declared prefix, and repeat independent trials until a prespecified confidence/precision or safety stopping rule is met. Log request arrival, queue entry/exit, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, every decode step, completion, cancellation, timeout, and error timestamps. Define TTFT as arrival-to-first-token and also report service-only TTFT; define TPOT with its generated-token denominator and state treatment of the first-token interval. Report queue-time distributions, request/token throughput, goodput denominator, and P99 end-to-end latency, stratified by input length, output length, concurrency, and burstiness. Measure prefill and decode separately; collect GPU utilization/memory, KV-cache occupancy, CPU load, power, temperature/throttling, batching/cache events, OOMs, evictions, timeouts, and correctness. Confounders include length mix, arrival process, cache warmth, scheduler interference, version drift, and thermal state. Roll back for correctness or reliability regression, memory exhaustion, or a breached latency guardrail; generalize only with evidence from additional loads, models, and hardware.
risks: Queue-inclusive and service-only latency may be conflated.
Nonidentical request mix, cache state, or background load can invalidate pairing.
P99 and goodput can be unstable without fixed denominators, repetitions, and stopping rules.
evidence_required: Versioned model/runtime/workload manifest; randomized pairing and trial logs; request lifecycle traces; length/concurrency strata; GPU/KV/CPU/power/thermal telemetry; correctness/failure logs; repeated-trial uncertainty estimates.
